page.title: Stag Weekend Boat Itinerary in Marbella 2025: Day-by-Day Plan

data.meta_description: Plan the ultimate stag weekend boat itinerary in Marbella 2025. Day-by-day plan, boat options from €749, and insider tips for Puerto Banús.

faq.q: How much does a stag weekend boat rental in Marbella cost?
faq.a: For a group up to 11, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 costs €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours – all inclusive. If you want a larger statement boat with a free jet ski, the Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours. Other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86 are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: How many people can join a stag boat party in Marbella?
faq.a: Capacity depends on the boat. The Astondoa 40 takes up to 9 guests, the Azimut 39 up to 11, and the Mangusta 80 up to 12. For bigger groups, consider the Ferretti 94 (12 pax) or Canados 86 (12 pax). Always confirm the exact pax limit when booking – it’s enforced for safety.

faq.q: What’s included in the boat rental for a stag weekend?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs – you just show up and enjoy. The skipper handles navigation and anchoring, so you can focus on the party.

faq.q: Can we bring our own alcohol on board?
faq.a: Yes, you can bring extra drinks, but the standard package already includes beer, wine, cava, and soft drinks. If you plan to bring spirits, let us know in advance – we’ll make sure there’s enough ice and glassware. The skipper reserves the right to refuse service to anyone who’s clearly intoxicated.

faq.q: What’s the best itinerary for a 2-day stag boat weekend?
faq.a: Day 1: depart Puerto Banús at 11:00, head to Cabopino for lunch and swimming, then anchor at Cala del Faro for sunset. Day 2: cruise east to Cala Cortés, enjoy jet ski time (if on a Mangusta), then return via Marbella Marina. This balances party time with scenic stops and avoids long open-sea stretches.

faq.q: Do we need a deposit or ID to book?
faq.a: A 30% deposit secures your date, with the balance due 7 days before departure. You’ll need a valid passport or ID for each guest on the day – the skipper must have a passenger list. For last-minute bookings, contact us via WhatsApp and we’ll confirm availability within hours.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on our stag weekend?
faq.a: If the captain deems conditions unsafe, we’ll reschedule your charter for a later slot or offer a full refund. In practice, Marbella enjoys 300+ sunny days a year, and the summer months (June–September) are exceptionally stable. We monitor forecasts closely and keep you updated.

faq.q: Can we add water toys like a jet ski to any boat?
faq.a: The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) includes a jet ski free of charge. For other boats, we can arrange a jet ski or inflatable towable as an add-on – just ask when booking. Prices vary, but expect around €150–€250 per 30 minutes depending on the boat and season.

data.body_html:
Planning a stag weekend in Marbella? A boat day is the best way to celebrate – think private coves, cold beer, and the Costa del Sol sun. This 2025 itinerary gives you a day-by-day plan, concrete prices, and local stops that actually work. No fluff, just the details you need to lock in an unforgettable stag do.

Why a Boat Charter is the Stag Weekend MVP

Marbella’s coastline is made for boats. From Puerto Banús you can reach quiet anchorages like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés in under 30 minutes, leaving the crowded beaches behind. A private charter means your group has its own space, music, and drinks – no bar queues, no dress codes. Plus, the skipper handles navigation, so you can relax and celebrate.

Our boats depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella’s glamour. You’ll see superyachts, beach clubs, and the Sierra Blanca mountains as a backdrop. For a stag group, the boat rental options in Marbella range from nimble speedboats to 29-metre flybridges – all with a licensed skipper included.

Choosing the Right Boat for Your Stag Group

Your choice depends on group size and budget. Here’s a quick breakdown of our fleet:

For a classic stag group of 8–11, the Azimut 39 is a sweet spot – fast, stylish, and fits everyone. If you want to arrive in style and have a jet ski for the lads, the Mangusta 80 is the showstopper. For other boats, message us on WhatsApp for a tailored quote.

Day 1: Arrival and Sunset Cruise

Land at Málaga Airport (AGP), take a 40-minute transfer to Puerto Banús, and check into your accommodation. By late afternoon, you’re ready for a 2-hour sunset cruise. We recommend the Astondoa 40 – it’s compact, easy to board, and perfect for a relaxed first taste of the sea.

Depart at 18:00, head west towards Cabopino. The skipper will anchor near the dunes for a swim stop (water temps in June hit 21°C). Enjoy beer, cava, and snacks as the sun sets over the Mediterranean. Return to port by 20:00 – just enough time to freshen up for dinner at a beach club on the Golden Mile.

Day 2: Full-Day Adventure with Jet Ski

This is the main event. Book a full-day charter (8 hours) on the Azimut 39 or upgrade to the Mangusta 80 for the free jet ski. Depart at 10:00 from Puerto Banús. Head east towards Cala Cortés, a secluded cove near Marbella Marina – perfect for swimming and cliff jumping (if you’re brave).

Lunch is served on board: light snacks, fresh fruit, and plenty of drinks. After lunch, anchor at Cala del Faro for snorkelling and jet ski rides. The skipper will point out the best spots for photos with La Concha mountain in the background. Return to port around 18:00, tired and happy.

Pro tip: bring a waterproof speaker and a playlist. Our boats have Bluetooth sound systems, but a backup never hurts. And don’t forget sunscreen – the UV index in July hits 9+.

Day 3: Recovery and Short Cruise (Optional)

If your stag weekend is three days, or you want a lighter option, book a 2-hour morning cruise on the Dubhe or Mariah SX21 – both are open speedboats that seat 5. Perfect for a small group or for the lads who want one last adrenaline hit before flying home.

Cruise towards Estepona, a charming marina with a colourful old town. Anchor for a quick swim, have a final toast, and head back by 13:00. This leaves time for a late lunch and airport transfer. For a 2-day stag, skip this and head straight to brunch in Puerto Banús.

Cost Breakdown for a Stag Boat Weekend

Here’s what you can expect to spend, excluding accommodation and meals:

  • Sunset cruise (2h, Astondoa 40): €749 total – split between 9 lads = €83 each
  • Full-day charter (8h, Azimut 39): €2,299 total – split between 11 = €209 each
  • Mangusta 80 with jet ski (4h min): €4,719 total – split between 12 = €393 each
  • Optional tips for skipper: €50–€100 per day

All prices include VAT, so no surprises. If you want a bigger boat like the Ferretti 94 or K80, contact us for a custom quote – we’ll match your group size and budget.

Top Stag-Friendly Stops Along the Coast

Our skippers know every cove. Here are the proven favourites for stag groups:

  • Cabopino: Sandy beach, beach bar, shallow water – ideal for a first stop.
  • Cala del Faro: Rocky cove with clear water, great for snorkelling and cliff jumps.
  • Cala Cortés: Quiet, scenic, and close to Marbella – perfect for a midday swim.
  • Estepona: A longer cruise west, but worth it for the marina vibe and lunch spots.
  • Puerto Banús: The ultimate people-watching spot – anchor off the breakwater to see superyachts.

Your skipper will adapt the route based on weather and your group’s energy. If you want to party hard, we’ll keep the music up; if you want to chill, we’ll find a quiet bay. It’s your weekend.

Booking Tips for a Smooth Stag Weekend

Book early – June to August weekends sell out 2–3 weeks ahead. A 30% deposit secures your date, and the balance is due 7 days before. You’ll need a valid ID for each guest. If you’re flying in, we can arrange transfers from Málaga Airport to Puerto Banús (ask for a quote).

Check the weather forecast a few days before. If the captain cancels due to unsafe conditions, you’ll get a full refund or reschedule. We’ve only had a handful of cancellations in the last five years – Marbella’s climate is that good.

For any questions or to check availability, message us on WhatsApp. We respond fast, usually within the hour. And if you’re still comparing options, our main boat rental page has the full fleet and booking details.
